Reading MAM-parsed-plain

The MAM-parsed-plain JSON files are formed by parsing the Wikitext in the MAM Google Sheet with minimal post-processing.

Use plain when you want a representation that stays close to the MAM Google Sheet. Use plus when you want conveniences intended to simplify most application code.

This document covers:

  • File naming
  • Structure of the top level
  • Structure of a book39, chapter, and verse
  • Template and custom-tag objects
  • Common templates
  • Pseudo-verses

File naming

File names (e.g. A1-Genesis.json) start with two characters that identify the book (in the “24 books” sense) and provide a standard ordering. The first character (sec_char) comes from the set ABCDEF and indicates the section of Tanakh. The second character (book24_char) comes from the set 12345AC and indicates the book within that section.

Files are named {sec_char}{book24_char}-{EnglishName}.json:

Prefix Section Books
A1–A5 Torah Genesis, Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers, Deuteronomy
B1, B2, BA, BC Former Prophets Joshua, Judges, Samuel, Kings
C1–C3, CA Latter Prophets Isaiah, Jeremiah, Ezekiel, The 12 Minor Prophets
D1–D3 Wisdom Psalms, Proverbs, Job
E1–E5 Five Scrolls Song of Songs, Ruth, Lamentations, Ecclesiastes, Esther
F1, FA, FC Late Books Daniel, Ezra-Nehemiah, Chronicles

When book24_char is A or C, the file is for a book24 with sub-books (e.g. BA-Samuel has sub-books 1 Samuel and 2 Samuel). The letter B is not used in order to keep compatibility with a set of codes used for the 39-book system.

Top-level structure

{
  "header": {...},
  "book39s": [...]
}

Header

Key Type Description
book24_name string The name of this file’s book24.
sub_book_names array Array of sub-book names for this book24. (Empty if this book24 has no sub-books.)
chapter_counts array One object per book39, each with sub_book_name and chapter_count. (The sub_book_name will be null for a book39 that is not a sub-book, i.e. a book39 that is also a book24.)

Here’s the header for Job, a book24 has no sub-books:

{
  "book24_name": "ספר איוב",
  "sub_book_names": [],
  "chapter_counts": [{"sub_book_name": null, "chapter_count": 42}]
}

Here’s the header for Samuel, a book24 that has sub-books:

{
  "book24_name": "ספר שמואל",
  "sub_book_names": ["שמ\"א", "שמ\"ב"],
  "chapter_counts": [
    {"sub_book_name": "שמ\"א", "chapter_count": 31},
    {"sub_book_name": "שמ\"ב", "chapter_count": 24}
  ]
}

Book39 structure

{
  "book24_name": "ספר ישעיהו",
  "sub_book_name": null,
  "chapters": {...}
}
Key Type Description
book24_name string For a book39 that is not a sub-book, this is its name. For a book39 that is a sub-book, this is the name of the book24 to which this sub-book belongs.
sub_book_name string | null For a book39 that is not a sub-book, this is null. For a book39 that is a sub-book, this is its name.
chapters object Object keyed by chapter numbers; values are chapter objects.

Chapter structure

The chapters dict is keyed as follows:

Key Category Purpose
"0" Pre-chapter Wiki navigation templates, page setup
Hebrew numerals Normal verses Actual verse data
"תתת" Post-chapter Wiki footer templates, end-of-chapter markup

The keys for normal verses are Hebrew numerals conforming to the system that uses טו and טז for 15 and 16, avoiding the divine-name letter-pairs.

Verse (pseudo-verse) structure

Each verse is a 3-element array corresponding to the C, D, and E columns of the Google Sheet.

C Verse separator: parashah break or "__" for a plain space
D Verse label (מ:פסוק template): book name, chapter, verse, etc.
E Verse text with inline templates

Index 0 (Google column C): Verse separator

The contents at index 0 indicate how this verse is separated from the preceding verse. "__" is by far the most common value, indicating a plain space. More interesting values include:

Template Meaning
פפ Parashah petuchah (open paragraph)
סס Parashah setumah (closed paragraph)
מ:ספר חדש New book marker — marks the start of one of the 24 books with defined spacing. Not used for second halves of two-part books or individual Minor Prophets after Hosea.
מ:אין פרשה בתחילת פרק No parashah at chapter start — tags chapters that don’t begin with a visible parashah.

Additional parashah-related templates that may appear:

Template Meaning
פפפ Open parashah starting immediately on the next line (no blank line)
ססס Closed parashah inline — blank spaces mid-line with text before and after
סס2 Narrow closed parashah
פסקא באמצע פסוק Parashah division within a verse
מ:רווח בתרי עשר Spacing between Minor Prophets
מ:רווח לספר בתהלים Spacing between the 5 “books” of Psalms (Psalms 1, 42, 73, 90, 107)

The "//"​ strings sometimes sprinkled in index 0 are Wikitext line breaks from the Google Sheet.

Index 1 (Google column D): Verse label

The content at index 1 is empty [] for pseudo-verses. For normal verses, it is a list containing exactly one element: the מ:פסוק template labeling the verse, e.g. for Job 1:2:

[{"stmpl": "מ:פסוק|איוב|א|ב"}]

The three required parameters are book name (Hebrew alphabet string), chapter number (Hebrew numeral), and verse number (Hebrew numeral). Optional named parameters include סדר= (seder number) and עלייה= (Torah aliyah identification).

E column (index 2): Verse text

Contains the actual verse text as a mixed array of strings (Hebrew text with cantillation marks) and template objects (inline markup). Example (Job 1:1):

[
  "אִ֛ישׁ הָיָ֥ה בְאֶֽרֶץ־ע֖וּץ אִיּ֣וֹב שְׁמ֑וֹ וְהָיָ֣ה",
  {"stmpl": "מ:לגרמיה-2"},
  " הָאִ֣ישׁ הַה֗וּא תָּ֧ם וְיָשָׁ֛ר וִירֵ֥א אֱלֹהִ֖ים וְסָ֥ר מֵרָֽע׃"
]

Template objects in plain

The plain format uses three kinds of template objects:

1. Stringified template (stmpl)

Many templates are simple enough to appear as a pipe-delimited string:

{"stmpl": "מ:פסוק|איוב|א|ב"}

This represents the Wikitext {{מ:פסוק|איוב|א|ב}}. The first segment (before |) is the template name; remaining segments are positional arguments.

2. Parsed template tree (tmpl)

Longer and/or more complex templates appear as parse trees:

{
  "tmpl": [
    ["#בלי קטע:", {"stmpl": "שם הדף המלא"}],
    ["סימן"]
  ]
}

The first sub-array is the template name. Subsequent sub-arrays are the arguments, which may contain nested template “calls”.

3. Custom XML tag (custom_tag)

Wikitext custom XML tags that appear in pseudo-verses:

{"custom_tag": "noinclude"}
{"custom_tag": "/noinclude"}

Common templates in the E (verse text) column

For English and Hebrew descriptions of most templates, see the Templates tab of the MAM Google Sheet.

Ketiv/qere templates

Template Purpose
כו״ק Standard ketiv/qere. Param 1 = unpointed ketiv, param 2 = pointed qere.
קו״כ Post-maqaf ketiv/qere. Same params as כו״ק but used when the pair follows a maqaf.
מ:קו״כ-אם-2 Trivial ketiv/qere. Param 1 = pointed ketiv, param 2 = unpointed ketiv, param 3 = pointed qere. See its dedicated page.
כתיב ולא קרי Ketiv without qere. Param 1 = the ketiv.
קרי ולא כתיב Qere without ketiv. Param 1 = the qere.
מ:כו״ק מיוחד Special ketiv/qere. See its dedicated page.

The nine סוג= subtypes for מ:כו״ק מיוחד:

Type Meaning
כו״ק בין שני מקפים Ketiv/qere between two maqaf marks. See FOI section k1q1-mcom.
כו״ק כתיב מילה חדה וקרי תרתין מילין 1-atom ketiv, 2-atom qere. See the rows of FOI section k1q2sr labelled k1q2-sr-kqq.
כו״ק כתיב מילה חדה וקרי תרתין מילין בין שני מקפים Same as above but between maqaf marks. See the rows of FOI section k1q2sr labelled k1q2-sr-bcom.
כו״ק כתיב תרתין מילין וקרי מילה חדה 2-atom ketiv, 1-atom qere. See FOI section k2q1.
קו״כ כתיב מילה חדה וקרי תרתין מילין 1-atom ketiv, 2-atom qere, following maqaf. See the rows of FOI section k1q2sr labelled k1q2-sr-qqk.
כו״ק קרי שונה מהכתיב בשתי מילים 1-atom ketiv not strongly related to its 2-atom qere. See FOI section k1q2wr.
קו״כ קרי שונה מהכתיב בשתי מילים 1-atom ketiv not strongly related to its 2-atom qere, following maqaf. See FOI section k1q2ur.
כו״ק של שתי מילים בהערה אחת 2-atom ketiv, 2-atom qere. See FOI section k2q2.
כו״ק של שלוש מילים בהערה אחת 3-atom ketiv, 3-atom qere. See FOI section k3q3.

Current values observed for optional סוג= in מ:קו״כ-אם-2:

  • אל"ף נחה באמצע תיבה ולא נקראת
  • כתיב ה"א בסיומת של חולם
  • כתיב הוא קרי היא
  • כתיב חסר יו"ד בסיומת של קמץ ואחריו וי"ו
  • כתיב נער קרי נערה

Example of standard ketiv/qere:

{"stmpl": "קו\"כ|את|אַ֠תָּ֠ה"}

Special letter templates

Template Purpose
מ:אות-ג Large letter. Parameter is the letter along with any diacritical marks.
מ:אות-ק Small letter. Parameter is the letter along with any diacritical marks.
מ:אות תלויה Suspended (hung) letter. Parameter is the letter along with any diacritical marks.
מ:נו״ן הפוכה Reversed (inverted) nun.

Accent, vowel, and punctuation templates

Template Purpose
מ:לגרמיה-2 Legarmeh. The vertical line ׀ as legarmeh (part of the word’s cantillation). Shares Unicode with paseq but differs in function.
מ:פסק Paseq. The vertical line ׀ as paseq in the narrow sense, i.e. paseq as distinct from legarmeh.
מ:מקף אפור Gray maqaf. A maqaf that is only implicit in the manuscript. Appears only in poetic verses.
גלגל-2 Galgal. Distinguishes poetic from prose uses of Unicode YBY.
ירח בן יומו-2 Yeraḥ ben yomo. Distinguishes prose from poetic uses of Unicode YBY.
מ:אות מנוקדת Dotted letter/word. Marks words with masoretic dots above/below.

Multimark templates

Template Purpose
שני טעמים ... Formats the two extra marks (above-accent + patah) on the QUPO Decalogue words (פני and מתחת). Parameter is the above-accent (may use מ:טעם).
מ:טעם Accent extractor. Drops the first code point of its argument, allowing an accent to be specified on a dummy letter for readability. Currently only used inside שני טעמים ....
מ:טעם ומתג באות אחת Normalization-robust meteg for 10 cases where a below-accent and meteg share one letter.
מ:גרש ותלישא גדולה Combined geresh + telisha gedolah (2 words, 3 uses). No parameters.
מ:גרשיים ותלישא גדולה Combined gershayim + telisha gedolah (3 words, 4 uses). No parameters.
מ:כל קמץ קטן מרכא Font-rendering workaround for the word כל with qamats qatan and merkha in Taamey Frank CLM (2 occurrences: Ps 35:10, Prov 19:7).
מ:ירושלם Handles the masoretic spelling of Jerusalem without yod. Two params (vowel and accent of lamed).
מ:ירושלמה Like מ:ירושלם but for the directional form “to Jerusalem” (4 cases).

Choice templates

Most applications will need to make a choice between two or three options presented by these templates.

Template Purpose
מ:דחי Deḥi variation. Presents both stress-helped and non-stress-helped versions of a word.
מ:צינור Tsinnor variation. Presents both stress-helped and non-stress-helped versions of a word.
מ:קמץ Qamats variation. Named params: ד= (grammatical) and ס= (Sephardic tradition).
מ:כפול Dual-trope span. See its dedicated page.

Whitespace templates

Template Purpose
פפ / פפפ / סס / ססס Parashah petuhah / setumah variants.
מ:ששש Setumah-like section divider for the 8 shirah (song) sections in the 21 prose books; analogous to ססס.
ר1 Following stich on its own line, one indent. In 2 cases (Ps 70, 108) represents a closed parashah.
ר2 Following stich on its own line, two indents.
ר3 Following stich at line start, no indent.
ר4 New verse at line start, no indent.
ר0 Extra division point when a verse has an odd number of stiches, for even-column display.
רווח בסוף שורה Large end-of-line spacers supporting פפפ; fills remaining line space so the next parashah can start at the top of the following line.

Many editions will choose to skip poetic formatting by treating ר0–ר4 as simple word spaces.

Note template

Template Purpose
מ:הערה Non-targeted scroll-difference note (Torah and Esther only). See Wikisource template page for מ:הערה.

Documentation templates

Template Purpose
נוסח Documentation template. See its dedicated page.
מודגש Bold text within the notes argument (param 2) of נוסח.
ש Paragraph separator within the notes argument (param 2) of נוסח.

Other templates

Template Purpose
מ:סיום בטוב Good ending. See its dedicated page.
פרשה-מרכז Centered title. For “titles” in Job and Proverbs. Parameter is the title text.

Pseudo-verses (0 and תתת)

The "0" and "תתת" keys are pseudo-verses that contain Wiki-specific navigation and formatting markup, not biblical text. They can generally be skipped when extracting verse content.

  • "0": Contains noinclude tags, navigation templates, margin settings.
  • "תתת": Contains end-of-chapter markers, unnumbered-verse section.
